## What This Experiment Tests

Published-prior cohort variant of `vector_unequal_width` with explicit `learnable=True` MoG prior declaration, testing transfer consistency across minor prior-contract differences. Four equal-mass corner Gaussians with distinct widths sigma in {0.07, 0.12, 0.20, 0.30}. Probes Law 3A (W1 ray-length identifiability): the trainer must match each cluster's individual width without smearing narrow clusters or shrinking broad ones.

> [!NOTE]
> **Protocol notes:** Separate published transfer cohort of `vector_unequal_width`; historical sensitivity observed across architectures.

## Laws & Edge Cases Targeted

- **[Law 1: Representational Geometry](../LAWS_HUB.md#law1)** ([Law 1 theory](../../../docs/four-laws.md#law-1--representational-geometry)) — Can the system represent the required probability measure efficiently and faithfully?
- **[Law 3A: Unconditional W1 Ray-Length & Screening Identifiability](../LAWS_HUB.md#law3a)** ([Law 3A theory](../../../docs/four-laws.md#law-3--transport-identifiability)) — Does the learning system possess enough information to determine appropriate transport?
- **Edge-case tags:** `multi-scale-width`, `ray-length-ambiguity`, `covariance-calibration`, `published-cohort`

## Common Failure Mode

Unit-slope W1/Lipschitz critics exert width-independent pull, collapsing wide clusters or letting stray samples contaminate the narrowest sigma=0.07 mode.
